svg.title: How Fabric Capacity Smoothing and Throttling Actually Work
svg.desc: A flow diagram tracing CU cost from submission through interactive vs background classification, bursting above SKU provision, 30-second timepoint smoothing (5-64m interactive, 24h background), and the progressive four-stage throttling ladder: overage protection, 20s delay, interactive rejection, and background rejection with carryforward burndown.
svg.text: Fabric Capacity — Bursting, Smoothing & Throttling Ladder
How CU consumption is spread over 30-second timepoints and enforced across 4 progressive stages

g.title: Operation submitted to capacity — Every workload draws Capacity Units from one dedicated resource pool.
g.text: • Interactive DAX visual, notebook execution, pipeline ETL, or warehouse query
• Sourced against the workspace's assigned F-SKU capacity unit (CU) quota

g.title: Classify: interactive vs background — Fabric classifies the operation before it runs, which sets its smoothing window.
Bursting — The operation is allowed to consume more CUs than steady-state SKU size allows, to finish quickly.
g.text: • Jobs exceed provisioned SKU rate without stalling, finishing at maximum speed
• 0 execution penalty in the moment — burst cost is deferred to smoothing
Spark burst multiplier grants up to 3x steady-state vCores (CU × 2 × 3)

g.title: Smoothing (30-second timepoints) — Bursted CU cost is spread across future timepoints instead of charged all at once.
g.text: • Spreads large spikes across future timepoints to prevent instantaneous throttle
✓ Accumulated smoothed cost forms the Future Usage balance checked in Phase 2

svg.text: PHASE 2: THE FOUR-STAGE PROGRESSIVE THROTTLING LADDER

g.title: Overage-protection check (10-minute window) — The decision point: is accumulated future usage under or over the 10-minute threshold?
g.text: Evaluates accumulated future CU debt: <10m (Normal) vs >10m (Escalating Enforcement)

g.title: No throttling — Under the 10-minute overage window: operations proceed normally with no visible impact.
g.text: • Future usage consumed: < 10 minutes of SKU provision.
• All interactive & background operations execute with 0 delay and 0 rejection.

g.title: Stage 2: interactive delay — Between 10 minutes and further thresholds: new interactive operations are delayed, not rejected.
g.text: • New interactive requests delayed by 20s. Background operations unaffected.

g.title: Stage 3: interactive rejection — Further past threshold: new interactive requests are rejected with CapacityLimitExceeded.
g.text: • Future usage consumed: 60 minutes to 24 hours.
• New interactive requests rejected outright. In-flight queries run to completion.

g.title: Stage 4: background rejection too — Worst stage: background operations are rejected as well, in addition to interactive ones.
g.text: • Both interactive AND background jobs rejected. Hard capacity exhaustion.
Surfaces error code 24801 / CapacityLimitExceeded to all callers

g.title: Burndown and carryforward drain — Carryforward CUs recorded during throttling drain only at timepoints with idle capacity.
g.text: • Throttling state is a running variable tracking accumulated future CU debt.
• At each future 30s slice, unconsumed capacity burns down carryforward debt.
• Capacity stays throttled until carryforward balance drains completely to zero.
Fan-out requests (Report ➔ Semantic Model ➔ OneLake) throttled at most ONCE per capacity.
✓ In-flight operations always allowed to finish regardless of throttling stage
Sourced from Microsoft Fabric Capacity Throttling & Smoothing Architecture.

g.aria-label: Autoscale Billing for Spark bypasses this entirely
g.title: Autoscale Billing for Spark bypasses this entirely — When enabled, Spark drops bursting and smoothing for flat pay-as-you-go metering.
g.text: • Autoscale Billing moves Spark to Azure pay-as-you-go metering.
• Drops 24h background smoothing protection; billed immediately per second.
Remedy: Size standard Spark pool before toggling autoscale billing.

g.aria-label: Private links and Direct Lake compatibility
g.title: Private links and Direct Lake compatibility — Block Public Internet Access breaks Direct Lake regardless of throttling state, and private link propagation takes up to 24h.
g.text: Network Setting Breaks Direct Lake Independent of CU
• Enabling "Block Public Internet Access" permanently severs Direct Lake models.
• Adding a new capacity with private links requires up to 24h for DNS sync.
Remedy: Verify tenant network routing rules before capacity rollout.

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — Original Infographic, August 2026. Grounded in Microsoft Fabric Capacity Architecture & Throttling Specs.
